question.problem:
Which of the following statements are true?

I. Any $3\times 4$ matrix $A$ has at most $4$ distinct singular values.

II. Any $8\times 6$ matrix $A$ has at most $8$ distinct singular values.

III. The matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]$ has one negative singular value.
question.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

With that in mind, let's examine our statements.

- Statement I is true. Since $A$ is a $3\times 4$ matrix and ${A}^{T}$ is a $4\times 3$ matrix, ${A}^{T}\,A$ must be a $4\times 4$ matrix: 

$$
{{A}^{T}}_{4\times 3}\times {A}_{3\times 4}={{A}^{T}\,A}_{4\times 4}
$$

Hence, $A$ has at most $4$ distinct singular values.

- Statement II is false. Since $A$ is a $8\times 6$ matrix and ${A}^{T}$ is a $6\times 8$ matrix, ${A}^{T}\,A$ must be a $6\times 6$ matrix: 

$$
{{A}^{T}}_{6\times 8}\times {A}_{8\times 6}={{A}^{T}\,A}_{6\times 6}
$$

Hence, $A$ has at most $6$ distinct singular values.

- Statement III is false.  All singular values of any matrix are non-negative. So, 
$A$  can't have a negative singular value.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."
